ai_show_review.summary: Intimate acoustic set, strong Jerry but muddy tape
ai_show_review.blurb: The brief acoustic set features Deep Elem Blues and Black Peter, highlighting Jerry Garcia's folk‑style vocals and guitar. While the performance feels intimate, the audience recording is saturated, hissy, and frequently distorted, limiting overall clarity.
ai_show_review.review: On May 9 1970 at Worcester Polytechnic Institute the Dead slipped into a short acoustic set that still manages to capture some of the band's early charm. Jerry Garcia’s pure folk‑style voice and deft guitar work shine on Deep Elem Blues and the haunting rendition of Black Peter, offering a rare glimpse of his unadorned storytelling before the band launches into their electric hour (which unfortunately isn’t captured on this tape). The set also includes Friend Of The Devil and Silver Threads And Golden Needles, but the recording itself is a muddied, hiss‑filled audience capture that sounds more like a cassette mic feed than a proper soundboard. Listeners will have to tolerate occasional overloads and dropouts, yet the intimacy of the performance still rewards those who appreciate Jerry’s early acoustic prowess.

best_recording.reason: Only known recording of the acoustic portion; despite poor quality it preserves Jerry's standout vocals and guitar.
